concepts.hidden_concept: Weighted / combined rate: you cannot average two group speeds; the bigger group pulls the result toward its own speed.
Scaling preserves the ratio: multiply every ingredient by the same factor; unknown amounts follow from the known one via the ratio.
Additive difference is not multiplicative ratio: a constant gap means a shrinking ratio as the numbers grow.
Part-to-part versus part-to-whole: a ratio 5:3 means 5/8 of the whole, not 5/3 and not '5 out of 10'.
Comparing mixtures needs a common basis: compare unit rates or fractions of the whole, not raw amounts.
Scale factor applies to every dimension equally: width and height scale by the same ratio of corresponding lengths.
Proportional allocation with whole numbers: exact shares may not be integers, and rounding must not break the total.
